transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I'm here because I keep snapping at people. Just... losing my temper. Like at this safety meeting we had, I... I started yelling before I could really stop myself. And now the younger inspectors act like they're scared to even ask me anything. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking through the consequences?
I don't think so. I mean... no. Just the yelling, like I said. I don't go around doing reckless things, if that's what you mean. It's just my temper.
Do you have trouble controlling other emotions, like sadness or anxiety, or is it mainly anger?
No... I don't think so. I'm not really a crier or anything. It's mostly just... the anger.
When did you first notice you were having trouble with your temper?

It's been a while. Um... about two years and four months, I guess. It started after... well, after that machinery accident. The one that happened right after they switched us to the overnight schedule.
Have you noticed yourself acting impulsively in situations that don't involve anger?
No... I haven't. Like I said a minute ago, I'm not reckless. It's really just the temper.
Have you ever done something impulsive that didn't involve yelling or anger?
No... I just said that. I don't do impulsive things. It's just the anger.
Do you have any habits or behaviors that you feel are compulsive or hard to control, aside from your temper?
No. I don't. I'm not sure why we keep going over this... I don't have any other habits like that. It's really just the temper.
Are there any specific behaviors or actions that you feel compelled to repeat over and over?
No. I don't do that. I don't know why you're asking me the same thing again... I don't have any weird habits or compulsions. I just... I get mad sometimes. That's it.
Have you ever found yourself doing something on impulse that didn't involve anger?
Look... I feel like we're just going in circles now. No. I don't do things on impulse. I really don't have anything else to tell you about that.
Do you find that your temper problems happen more often in certain situations or when you're under a lot of stress?

I don't know if it's stress. I just... I'm here because I keep snapping at people. Like at work... we had a safety meeting and I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. Now the younger inspectors act scared to ask me anything. It just happens.
Do you think the machinery accident you mentioned earlier triggered your temper problems?

I suppose. Yeah... that's when it started. It was right after that machinery accident... they had just put us on an overnight schedule change. So... it's been about two years and four months now. It's just been going on since then.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with others since your temper problems started?

...I suppose. I mean, I already mentioned work. It's... well, I've missed a lot of shifts lately. And I lost so much patience with the trainees that... they just don't trust me to mentor the younger inspectors anymore. So that's gone. 

And... I don't know. Outside of work, I used to do community theater. But I pulled back from it. I just... I can't reliably get through the rehearsals now. So it's just easier not to be around people.
Have you ever felt like you're taking risks or acting impulsively in other areas of your life, outside of your temper?
No... I don't think so. I just... I don't really do much of anything right now. Just work and home. So... no. Not really.
Do you feel like your temper outbursts have become a habitual response to certain situations
I don't know... I haven't really thought about it like that. I just... get mad sometimes. I don't think it's a habit or anything. It just happens.
Do you think you learned this pattern of getting angry from someone else, like a family member or someone you work with?
No... I don't think so. My family wasn't really like that. And work is... well, people get frustrated, but... no. I don't think I learned it from anyone. It's just... me, I guess.
Do you think getting angry is a way for you to cope with stress or difficult situations?
I don't know... I don't really look at it like that. I just... when things get to be too much, I get mad. I wouldn't call it coping. It doesn't really help anything. It just... happens.
Would you describe yourself as having a generally aggressive or confrontational personality even outside of these anger outbursts?
No... I wouldn't say that. I just do my job and go home. I don't go looking for fights.
Do you think your anger outbursts are part of who you are as a person?
I don't... I don't know. I mean, I guess it's me doing it, so... maybe? But I don't really think about it like that. It's just what happens.
Do you feel like your temper outbursts have become an automatic response to certain situations without you even thinking about it?

Yeah... I guess so. I mean, that's kind of why I'm here. I just... I keep snapping at people. Like at this safety meeting recently... I just started yelling before I could even stop myself. It just came out. And now... I don't know, the younger inspectors, they act like they're scared to even ask me anything. So... yeah. I guess it is.
Do you feel like you have no control over your temper outbursts when they happen

Yeah... I guess I don't. Like I said... that safety meeting. I just yelled. Didn't even think about it, it just happened. And now... well, those younger ones, they just stay away. They're scared to ask me questions. So... no, I don't really have control when it happens.
